ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Commercial Act, as amended, Articles 543 through 583 governing Yuhan Hoesa; the Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information (FTRA), as amended; the Real Name Financial Transactions and Confidentiality Act, as amended; the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, as amended; and applicable Korean Financial Intelligence Unit and Financial Supervisory Service customer due diligence and beneficial ownership rules implementing AML/CFT standards.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Certificate of Registered Matters or Company Registration Certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry Office of the District Court with jurisdiction over the registered office, operated through the Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (IROS)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Issued by the Korean court registry; notarized copy before a Korean notary if required; then, if destination state is an Apostille Convention member, the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) must issue an Apostille. If the destination state is not an Apostille Convention member, the document must receive MOFA consular authentication and then legalization by the destination state's consular officer in Korea. The Apostille route and consular legalization route are parallel and mutually exclusive; they must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or Tax Compliance Letter
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea or the District Court Registry, as applicable
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Copy must be obtained from the National Tax Service or court registry, notarized if required, and then either (a) apostilled by MOFA for use in a Hague Apostille Convention country or (b) processed through MOFA consular authentication followed by consulate or embassy legalization in non-Hague destination. Use one path only, never both.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Board Resolution and Power of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of each foreign shareholder, notarized in the shareholder's origin country or before a Korean notary public for Korean-resident signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Board resolution and power of attorney must be notarized in the country of origin; if that country is a Hague Convention member, affix an Apostille from that country's competent authority. If that country is not a Hague member, execute consular legalization through the Korean diplomatic mission. A parallel Korean notarization is acceptable but the document must not be double-authenticated under both Apostille and consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association of the Yuhan Hoesa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Founding shareholders and the Korean notary public who authenticates the signatures on the articles
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For certified copies of the Articles of Association, use notarization and then MOFA Apostille if the receiving authority is in a Hague Convention state; for non-Hague states, use MOFA consular authentication followed by the receiving state's embassy or consulate legalization in Korea. Do not chain Apostille with consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for each non-resident shareholder or the company being formed
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Originating bank of the non-resident shareholder or the intended Korean bank, issued on bank letterhead with bank officer signature
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The bank reference letter must be notarized in the bank's jurisdiction. If the bank is in a Hague member state, obtain an Apostille from that jurisdiction. If the bank is in a non-Hague state, obtain consular legalization by the Korean embassy or consulate before acceptance. The two procedures are mutually exclusive alternatives; never stack them sequentially.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Screening must be completed before any relationship begins and must cover all incorporators, shareholders, directors, beneficial owners, signatories, and any person holding 25 percent or more through trusts, chains, or bearer structures. The protocol requires continuous matching against the United Nations Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, Korean FIU watch lists, Korea Customs Service notices, and government-issued domestic blacklists. PEP screening must cover immediate family members and close associates of current or former senior foreign officials. Every positive hit triggers enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth verification, independent media review, and a suspicious transaction report to the Korean FIU where legally required. All screening records must be retained for at least five years after termination of the relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Internet Registration Office (IRO) of the Supreme Court of the Republic of Korea (https://www.iros.go.kr)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Commercial Act, the trade name of a Yuhan Hoesa must be expressed in Hangeul in the corporate register. A foreign-language name may be used secondarily only after phonetic transliteration into Hangeul and acceptance by the registry. The statutory naming convention has four parts: the identifying trade name, the business-object clause, the legal-form suffix Yuhan Hoesa representing a limited liability company, and the registered office address. Romanized or Latin-script-only names are not sufficient as the sole registered corporate name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the registry rejects the proposed name, the applicant receives a written statement of grounds and a short correction window. The applicant may, within fourteen days, submit a written objection through IROS or to the competent district court registration office, attaching the corrected Hangeul name, a clear business-purpose clause, and any relevant ministerial approvals for prohibited or sensitive tokens. If the objection is dismissed, the applicant may initiate an administrative appeal to the Registration Examination Division or an administrative lawsuit under the Administrative Litigation Act. It is prudent to reserve an alternative name simultaneously.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A bare virtual office or commercial mailbox is not permissible as the registered office for a South Korean Yuhan Hoesa engaged in an offshore software development center. The National Tax Service and commercial banks require an observable physical site where ODC personnel, equipment, software infrastructure, business records, and management are based. A co-working office is acceptable only if the company has a dedicated lockable workspace, its own nameplate, a lease agreement registered in the company's name, recurring utility invoices, and physical employees during normal hours. Without these elements, corporate bank onboarding and tax registration may be refused due to insufficient commercial substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for unannounced tax and registry inspection: (1) original lease contract and current rent invoices, (2) company nameplate and signage, (3) employees present during declared business hours, (4) ODC server workstations and documentation, (5) statutory books, accounting records and tax filings, (6) corporate seal and registration certificates, (7) bank statements and payment-rail contracts, and (8) electricity, Internet and facility contracts. Quantified risk: moderate-to-high probability of 50 to 70 percent physical inspection within the first 12 months after registration for a newly formed ODC, rising to roughly 85 percent within 36 months if no employees, no tax filing, or an unverifiable virtual office is detected.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Korean commercial registry incorporation fee for Yuhan Hoesa
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: District Court Registry (Supreme Court of Korea)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee fixed under Korean court fee and commercial registration regulations for an LLC with zero or low stated capital.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: National Tax Service business registration certificate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No official fee for issuance of a business registration certificate.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company name search and preliminary availability review at IROS
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No official fee for electronic name search and reservation review.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of articles of association, board resolutions and power of attorney
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Korean notary public or foreign notary in shareholder jurisdiction
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notary fee schedule under the Korean Notary Act and market rate per notarized signature and Korean page.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation and authentication of shareholder and corporate documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Certified translation provider and Korean consular authorities abroad
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market rate per notarized page plus official consular fees; non-Hague states incur additional legalization fees.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official Apostille fee per document under Korean Apostille issuance rules.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Commercial landlord or co-working operator in Seoul

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended); Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company) provisions, principally Articles 543 to 601, together with the Supreme Court Regulations on Registration and the Notary Public Act for authentication of Articles of Incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registration Division of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office; online filing through the Korean Internet Registration Office (iRO) operated by the Supreme Court of Korea.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Yuhan Hoesa (Limited Liability Company), filed with notarized Articles of Incorporation and capital contribution evidence.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None - no statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed for a Yuhan Hoesa. The Articles of Incorporation state the capital amount agreed by the members; cash contributions must be fully paid and evidenced, and in-kind contributions must be appraised. There is no government-mandated blocked escrow account requirement, though paid-in capital must be traceable to the company account before registration is completed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF YUHAN HOESA. At a duly convened first meeting of the Board of Directors of Yuhan Hoesa (the Company), held at the Company's registered office on [date] at [time], the following directors were present: [names], constituting a quorum in accordance with the Korean Commercial Act and the Company's Articles of Incorporation. The Chairperson, having been duly elected and having confirmed that notice of the meeting had been waived by all persons entitled to receive such notice, declared the meeting validly constituted. RESOLVED, that the subscription of the entire issued share capital of the Company, in the total stated amount of KRW [amount], be and is hereby approved and ratified; that the allocation of contributions set forth in the register of members is confirmed; and that each subscriber's contribution has been fully paid in cash or in permitted in-kind property, free of any lien or set-off, in accordance with the applicable provisions of the Korean Commercial Act. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company be and is hereby fixed at [registered office address], Republic of Korea, and that all statutory books, records, and public notices required under Korean law be maintained at that address. RESOLVED, that [Bank name], [branch], be and is hereby designated as the Company's principal banker; that [Name], [Name], and [Name], or any one of them as determined by the Board, be and hereby are authorized, jointly or singly, to open, operate, close, and mandate ordinary, foreign currency, electronic, wire transfer, and B2B payment accounts in the name of the Company; to execute bank mandates, signatory cards, online banking agreements, standing orders, loan documents, and indemnities; and to give lawful banking instructions for all Company funds, including Wise B2B, Payoneer, and wire payment rails. RESOLVED, that the following statutory officers be and hereby are appointed: [Name] as Representative Director (Chief Executive Officer), [Name] as Director of Engineering, and [Name] as Director of Finance, each to serve until the first general meeting of members following appointment and until a successor is duly elected, with the powers specified in Korean law and in the Articles of Incorporation. RESOLVED, that all directors are authorized to execute and file the Application for Registration of Incorporation, to pay all registration fees, to obtain business and tax registration certificates and corporate seals, to open bank accounts, and to do every lawful act necessary to complete the formation of the Company and to implement the resolutions set forth above.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate name search and notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean Internet Registration Office (iRO) at www.iros.go.kr; Korean Notary Public under the Notary Public Act.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Reserve the corporate name electronically to verify that the proposed name is distinguishable from existing Korean companies. Prepare, in Korean, the Articles of Incorporation, which must include the legal name, business scope (dedicated offshore software engineering and maintenance), registered office address, capital contribution schedule, director appointment clauses, and terms of dissolution. Submit the Articles to a Korean notary public for authentication; the notary must confirm personal appearance, identity, and signatures of the incorporators. If a non-resident member appoints a local agent or uses a power of attorney, the relevant Power of Attorney should be notarized, apostilled, or consular-legalized before the notarial appointment. In-kind contributions must be described and valued in the Articles or a separate valuation certificate.
required_dossiers: Proposed Articles of Incorporation in Korean
Passport copies of incorporators and directors
Notarization and legalization documents for foreign signatories
In-kind contribution valuation report, if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name search is refused or suspended, submit a revised distinguishable name and carry out a fresh search. If the notary raises a substantive defect, correct the Articles and re-attend notarial authentication; any foreign document lacking apostille or consularization must be legalized before re-submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registration Division of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the incorporation registration application with the District Court Registration Division within three weeks after notarization. Submit the notarized Articles of Incorporation, the application for registration of incorporation, evidence that the capital contributions have been fully made and credited, written consent of each director and statutory officer, and identification documents of all incorporators. Where submission is made by a representative or administrative agent, execute and attach a power of attorney. Pay the applicable registration license tax, local education tax, and court registration fee and obtain the receipt. Upon examination and entry of the registration, request the issuance of the Certificate of Registered Matters and the corporate seal report. Thereafter, the company exists as a legal entity and may begin pre-registration preparatory acts.
required_dossiers: Application for Registration of Incorporation of Yuhan Hoesa
Bank certificate or statement evidencing paid-in capital
Consent forms of directors and statutory officers
Power of attorney and agent identification, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a supplementary instruction or suspension, cure the defect by filing an amendment or supplemental document within two weeks; if dismissed, the incorporators may re-file with a corrected application and pay the fee again.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Business Registration with the tax office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local District Tax Office (under the National Tax Service) having jurisdiction over the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month after court registration, apply for the Corporate Business Registration at the district tax office of the registered office. Submit the Certificate of Registered Matters, notarized Articles of Incorporation, lease agreement for the registered office, corporate seal, and the representative director's identification. Ask the tax office to issue the taxable business registration certificate for corporate income tax, value-added tax, employee withholding, and payroll-related insurance. Because the business is a zero-rated software export service, register the entity for foreign currency and B2B invoicing rails and report the place of business. After issuance, open the corporate bank account and file the actual place of business with the tax office. The business registration certificate and tax invoice number must be retained for all future Korean tax filings.
required_dossiers: Corporate seal and seal reporting card
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office queries the registered office or business purpose, provide the lease agreement and an explanatory letter describing ISIC 6202; if a defect in seal documentation arises, obtain a new seal report and resubmit the application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign exchange bank account and foreign direct investment notification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Designated Foreign Exchange Bank; Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency Invest Korea under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the foreign exchange and foreign direct investment compliance immediately after tax registration. If a non-resident subscribes capital or funds the Company, submit a Foreign Investment Notification under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act to a designated foreign exchange bank or through the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency Invest Korea before making the equity contribution. After notification, open a foreign currency corporate account in the Company's legal name and execute the banking resolution approved by the Board. Provide the bank with the Certificate of Registered Matters, business registration certificate, source-of-funds declarations, and beneficial ownership information. For ongoing operations using Wise B2B, Payoneer, or wire rails, instruct the bank to apply the standard low-risk customer due diligence protocol and retain all foreign exchange transaction reports in accordance with the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.
required_dossiers: Beneficial ownership and bank account signatory information
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the designated bank or Invest Korea suspends the Foreign Investment Notification, correct the shareholding or business purpose data and provide a detailed source-of-funds explanation; if an exchange penalty is threatened, consult a Korean tax attorney or certified public accountant to regularize the filing before the deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial licensing and environmental applicability screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Employment and Labor and National Fire Agency for ordinary office premises; no industrial licensing agency for ISIC 6202.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a formal industrial licensing screen to document that ISIC 6202 computer programming and software consultancy is a pure digital activity. Confirm that the offshore development center operates no manufacturing, assembly, chemical processing, warehousing, or physical product handling, and therefore no industrial operating license, Environmental Impact Assessment tier, or Civil Defense fire permit is required. Retain the ISIC 6202 business scope statement, the Certificate of Registered Matters, and the business registration certificate in the corporate compliance file. For the ordinary office lease, follow the Basic Fire Safety inspection duties and Occupational Safety and Health Act obligations, including maintaining a small fire extinguisher and posting business identification. No further industrial environmental permit is required for the offshore development center as structured.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a local authority incorrectly assumes a manufacturing license is needed, provide the ISIC 6202 classification letter and certificate of business scope; if a landlord or client requests environmental proof, issue a written confirmation that the offshore development center is non-industrial and no Environmental Impact Assessment tier applies.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - no physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing operations exist under ISIC 6202.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - no EIA screening, full EIA report, or environmental registration is required for a pure digital software engineering and maintenance hub.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - no industrial wastewater, VOC emissions, or hazardous waste generation arises from ISIC 6202 computer programming and consultancy activities.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - no Civil Defense fire permit or industrial fire safety permit is required. Ordinary leased-office occupational safety and fire prevention obligations under the Occupational Safety and Health Act and applicable building fire safety regulations may still apply.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; electronic portal: HomeTax (hometax.go.kr); Korea Customs Service (KCS) via UNI-PASS for export clearance; Foreign Investment Ombudsman / Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) for foreign investment reporting.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-invested Korean Yuhan Hoesa, if the non-resident investor acquires 10% or more of voting shares, file a Foreign Investment Report with the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy through KOTRA under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and obtain a Foreign Investment Report Certificate. Incorporate the legal entity under the Commercial Act at the local court registry; then apply for Business Registration with the competent district tax office within one month of business commencement under the Framework Act on National Taxes, presenting the certificate of incorporation, articles of association, share-capital remittance certificate, leased place of business contract, and foreign investment report certificate. NTS issues a Business Registration Certificate containing the 10-digit Business Registration Number (BRN), which functions as the corporate Tax Identification Number (TIN) and VAT registration number; the BRN is activated in HomeTax. For a non-resident company without a Korean place of business that makes Korean VAT-taxable supplies, the non-resident must register as a non-resident business operator under Article 53 of the Value-Added Tax Act through a tax representative in Korea and is issued a supplier tax code for VAT purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None for US-style check-the-box; Yuhan Hoesa is a per se entity-level taxpayer under the Corporate Income Tax Act. Korean tax law permits election of consolidated corporate tax filing (group taxation) for a domestic parent and wholly-owned domestic subsidiaries, and election of tax exemption/reduction for foreign-invested companies under the Special Cases of Taxation Act. Hybrid mismatch elections are not offered; Korea applies OECD hybrid-mismatch rules through the International Tax Adjustment Act and tax treaty anti-abuse provisions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: KRW 0 - registration is mandatory for every domestic corporation from the commencement of business regardless of turnover; no statutory turnover threshold exists for Yuhan Hoesa. Non-resident suppliers of electronic services to Korean consumers are also required to register for VAT without a de minimis threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Under Article 32 of the Value-Added Tax Act and NTS e-Sacgi regulations, all B2B suppliers must issue and transmit electronic tax invoices to HomeTax using structured XML/API by the day after the supply amount is settled; NTS operates near-real-time automated cross-verification. B2C supplies require cash receipts through the mandatory Cash Receipt System. No physical fiscal stamping device is used; the e-invoice is the fiscal clearance act.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 24 of the Value-Added Tax Act and Article 31 of its Enforcement Decree, exports of goods are zero-rated. Services, including offshore software engineering/maintenance, are zero-rated when supplied to a non-resident who receives the services wholly outside Korea, the consideration is paid in convertible foreign currency, and documentary evidence of export is retained. The Korean ODC must issue a valid electronic tax invoice (export), and the corresponding foreign exchange receipt must be evidenced.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export Declaration issued and accepted by the Korea Customs Service through UNI-PASS where physical goods or media are exported
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing cargo movement from Korea to the foreign destination when physical goods are involved
Written Offshore Dev Center Services Contract between KR_YUHANGHOESA and the non-resident client, defining scope, deliverable location, terms and payment in foreign currency
Commercial Invoice in convertible foreign currency matching the contractual services and bank receipts
Foreign Exchange Receipt Certificate (equivalent to Inward Remittance Certificate, FIRC) issued by a Korean foreign exchange bank confirming the export proceeds were received in foreign currency
Electronic Tax Invoice / e-Sacgi for the zero-rated supply, transmitted to the NTS via HomeTax
Bank remittance advice and any supplementary evidence of actual use of the software/service by the foreign principal outside Korea
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: NTS can deny the 0% rate where export and FX documentation is absent or inconsistent; the company becomes liable for 10% VAT, plus additional tax of up to 60% of the tax due for cheating under the Framework Act on National Taxes, and a 2% added tax for an unverifiable false e-tax invoice under Article 69 of the Value-Added Tax Act. Fraudulent zero-rating claims are subject to criminal sanctions (imprisonment or up to 3 times evaded VAT) and retrospective clawback of input VAT credits. Failure to repatriate export proceeds within the statutory 540-day period triggers administrative fines and interest under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK), with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) as the foreign exchange administration authority under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Korean won (KRW) is convertible for current-account transactions, and software development and export service fees may be collected in foreign currency and held in Korean foreign-currency deposit accounts. Korea does not impose mandatory surrender or fixed conversion quotas on export proceeds; receipt, retention, and repatriation are processed through banks supervised by the Bank of Korea. Capital-account transactions, including foreign direct investment into the Korean LLC, are not unregulated; they require a notification or declaration under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, but eligible software engineering services do not require investment approval. The initial equity contribution must be linked to a Foreign Investment Promotion Act notification filed before the inward wire through an authorized foreign-exchange bank or KOTRA. Dividends and branch profits may be remitted after corporate tax settlement using audited financial statements, tax clearance, shareholders' resolutions, and remittance evidence reviewed by the settlement bank. The practical constraints are documentary and procedural rather than prohibitive: every cross-border remittance needs an underlying contract or invoice, a purpose code, a domestic bank relationship, and positive due diligence results. There are no balance-of-payments restrictiveness penalties for a properly notified offshore development center, and no requirement to force KRW conversion at a below-market rate.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: The Foreign Exchange Transactions Regulations require goods export proceeds to be collected generally within 180 days of the export customs date and service export proceeds generally within 90 days of service completion, or by the contractual due date if shorter; extensions may be granted by the foreign-exchange bank upon proper justification before the deadline. The mandatory surrender ratio is zero: exporters may retain 100 percent of foreign-currency receipts in a foreign-currency on-call deposit or designated account, and conversion to KRW is at the market rate. All receipts must be reported under the applicable balance-of-payments settlement code so the Bank of Korea can monitor abnormal delays, reversals, or trade-mismatch patterns.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: FDI Notification and Operational KRW Current Account
Foreign Currency Deposit Account plus KRW Operational Account
Global Trade Services Account for SWIFT LC and Remittance
Basic Operational Currency Account and Payroll Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Legally constrained. Wise Business and Payoneer are not licensed Korean banks and cannot open domestic KRW corporate accounts, issue local sort codes, or perform the statutory foreign-exchange reporting that the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act requires a local foreign-exchange bank to perform. They may be used only as auxiliary billing rails for small foreign-currency payments to overseas contractors; all statutory capital transactions, KRW settlements, Korean payroll, VAT payments, and profit remittances must be cleared through a Bank of Korea-supervised tier-1 commercial bank. No offshore EMI can serve as the primary treasury relationship for this ODC.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Tier-1 Korean banks require real-name verification and a compliance interview when onboarding a foreign-owned LLC. A non-resident statutory director does not have automatic standing to open remotely; in ordinary practice, either the director must appear physically in a Korean branch or the company must appoint a local authorized signatory with an Alien Registration Card under an apostilled and notarized power of attorney. Remote consular proxy opening alone is generally rejected because Korean anti-money laundering rules require the bank to positively identify the decision-maker and ultimate beneficial owner; the authorized signatory must complete a face-to-face or video-call KYC interview and present original corporate documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital from a non-Korean parent holding company in a low-substance jurisdiction triggers shell-structure suspicion.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Group structure chart; parent company incorporation and beneficial ownership register; UBO declaration listing all natural persons holding 25 percent or more; notarized passport copies; tax residence certificates; six months of parent bank statements; source-of-wealth letter; Korean LLC business plan; lease agreement and payroll records showing local operational substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign director or UBO cannot satisfy Korean real-name verification due to absence of an Alien Registration Card or local presence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid passport; proof of foreign address; apostilled corporate resolution appointing the director; notarized power of attorney appointing a resident authorized signatory; certified Korean translations of all identification and incorporation documents; completed bank real-name verification form; recorded video interview before the compliance officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: ODC revenue stream is exclusively intercompany service income, creating a pass-through or transfer-pricing money-laundering red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed offshore development services agreement with the parent or end clients; detailed statement of work and rate card; transfer pricing documentation; payroll and social insurance records for local employees; office lease and utility invoices; VAT invoices for local purchases; audited financial statements or projected profit-and-loss analysis; board minutes confirming the commercial substance of the ODC.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial FDI wire arrives without a matching Foreign Investment Promotion Act notification or a valid balance-of-payments purpose code, causing the funds to be quarantined.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Foreign Investment Notification certificate or confirmation from the receiving foreign-exchange bank; board resolutions of the investing entity and the Korean LLC approving the capital contribution; source and destination bank statements; MT103 with the correct FDI purpose code; draft articles of incorporation; evidence that the Korean entity will file annual foreign investment reports; statement of capital usage and local employment projections.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The foreign investor must first submit a Foreign Direct Investment notification under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act through KOTRA or an authorized foreign-exchange bank, receiving a Foreign Investment Notification certificate. The inward payment is then sent by SWIFT MT103 to the Korean ODC's domestic bank account, using the FDI purpose code and referencing the notification certificate. The receiving Korean bank posts the funds with the Bank of Korea's balance-of-payments reporting code, verifies the remitter against the notification, and issues or records the capital verification/foreign investment registration evidence. The ODC may convert the foreign exchange to KRW at the market rate without any mandatory surrender. If additional funding is structured as an intercompany loan, a separate Foreign Exchange Transactions Act loan report and repayment schedule must be filed before the inbound remittance.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: All outbound cross-border payments are cleared through a domestic licensed bank: SWIFT MT103 is used for direct service fees, royalties, subcontractor software development, and intercompany expense reimbursements; irrevocable commercial letters of credit and documentary collections are used for hardware, colocation equipment, and inventory purchases where title or shipment documents are necessary; local KRW vendor and payroll disbursements are executed via KFTC and BOK-Wire+ rails. Every disbursement must be backed by an underlying contract, invoice, or intra-group service agreement and registered with the bank under the appropriate foreign-exchange purpose code; the bank will reject any payment without supporting trade or service documentation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore forward FX contracts in USD/KRW and EUR/KRW for the LLC's documented current-account trade and service exposures
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) executed through a licensed Korean foreign-exchange bank when the underlying KRW exposure does not require physical settlement capacity
Cross-currency basis swaps permitted only when matched to an underlying foreign-currency intercompany loan or borrowings
FX options limited to hedging verified future receivables or payables; outright speculation is prohibited under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Base Return and Payment (Corporate Tax Act, Article 60; Framework Act on National Taxes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea through the HomeTax electronic filing system; local municipal tax office for the local surtax component
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the end of the business year; automatically extended to 4 months from year-end when the return is prepared and signed by an accredited Korean tax agent. For a 31 December year-end, the unextended deadline is 31 March and the extended deadline is 30 April.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file by the statutory deadline attracts an additional tax of 20% of the understated corporation tax base, or 40% if the shortfall is intentional or reckless; unpaid corporate tax accrues a daily delinquency charge at the statutory rate of 0.025% per day from the first day after the due date until full payment. Three consecutive business years of non-filing and non-payment will trigger seizure and public sale of assets, cancellation of the business registration by the National Tax Service, and, after court-ordered liquidation procedures, administrative strike-off or dissolution of the Yuhan Hoesa.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Corporate Income Tax Surcharge Return and Payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: The competent Metropolitan City, Special Self-Governing City, or Provincial Government tax authority via the Wetax local-tax e-filing portal.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the end of the business year, aligned with the National Tax Service corporate tax return; for a 31 December year-end, 31 March, or 30 April where the National Tax Service deadline has been extended by a tax agent.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or non-payment of the local corporate income tax surcharge triggers the Local Tax Act additional charge of 20% for non-compliant reporting, together with a daily delinquency charge at 0.025% per day. If the surcharge remains unpaid after demand, the local government may seize bank accounts and movable assets, register a tax lien, and ultimately force closure of the ODC business and judicial strike-off of the company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External Audit Report Filing under the Act on External Audit and Accounting of Stock Companies, where statutory thresholds are exceeded
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service through the DART system; the signed CPA audit report must also be attached to the annual corporate tax return filed with the National Tax Service.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after the close of the business year; for a 31 December year-end, the filing must be made not later than 30 April of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the external audit report on time subjects the representative director and responsible officers to administrative sanctions of up to KRW 20,000,000 (approximately USD 15,000) under the External Audit Act, and the report is excluded from the statutory financial-statement set, rendering the corporate tax return incomplete and subject to the 20% non-filing penalty.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting of Members and Approval of Financial Statements under the Commercial Act Yuhan Hoesa Chapter
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company registered office in the Republic of Korea; minutes must be preserved and made available to the National Tax Service, the external auditor, and the registered agent upon request.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the end of each business year; for a 31 December year-end, the ordinary general meeting must be convened on or before 31 March.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold the annual meeting or to approve the balance sheet and profit-and-loss statement within the statutory period exposes the directors to administrative and criminal fines under the Commercial Act; if financial statements are never approved, the external auditor cannot legally certify the tax return and the National Tax Service can disregard the annual accounts, leading to tax assessments, penalties, and eventual court-ordered dissolution or strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign Investment Status or Change Report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, applicable where a foreign investor owns 100% of the Yuhan Hoesa or any membership interest
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) and the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE); additional copy may be required by the registered agent.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Initial foreign investment report must be filed before or at the time of the investment; any subsequent transfer of membership interests, material change of registered facts, or change in foreign ownership percentage must be reported to KOTRA within 30 days of the event. There is no fixed annual KOTRA report, but the annual corporate tax return and the register of members must reconcile all foreign ownership data.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file a foreign investment report or change report within the 30-day window attracts a fine under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, loss of status as a foreign-invested enterprise, denial of dividend remittance guarantees and tax treaty protection, and application by the National Tax Service of the more restrictive domestic withholding rules on the offshore ODC payments.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Article 2 of the Act on External Audit and Accounting of Stock Companies and the relevant Presidential Decree, mandatory independent audit by a licensed Korean CPA firm is imposed if, at the end of the immediately preceding business year, the Yuhan Hoesa has: (1) total assets of KRW 12,000,000,000 (approximately USD 9,100,000) or more; (2) total assets of KRW 7,000,000,000 or more and is treated as a public-interest or large non-public company because of member count, borrowing structure, or licensor requirements; (3) annual operating revenue of KRW 10,000,000,000 or more together with an end-of-year debt-to-equity ratio above 150%; or (4) explicit contractual or regulatory demand for audited financial statements from its bank, registered agent, or ODC client contract. There is no standalone headcount threshold for external audit, but an ODC employing more than 250 full-time people may be reclassified as a large enterprise for Korean disclosure and consolidation purposes.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS), fully aligned with IFRS as adopted in Korea, for all companies required to obtain an external audit; Korean GAAP for Non-Public Entities and Korean SME Accounting Standards for smaller Yuhan Hoesa entities that do not cross the audit threshold.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: At the Korean corporate-registry level, no annual confirmation statement or annual UBO return is required for a private Yuhan Hoesa. Instead: (1) the Register of Members and corporate minute books must be continuously updated at the registered office; (2) any transfer of a membership interest must be recorded in the membership ledger and, if required by the articles or Commercial Act, registered in the commercial register; (3) if a foreign investor owns 10% or more of the entity, any change in ownership percentage, membership transfer, or UBO identity must be reported to KOTRA or MOTIE within 30 days; and (4) financial institutions and payment-rail counterparties such as Wise, Payoneer, and wire banks require annual beneficial-ownership re-verification under the Korean AML Act and FATF Standards, which operates as the de facto annual UBO confirmation.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (membership ledger of the Yuhan Hoesa)
Minute Book (general meetings and board meetings)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,800 - USD 4,200 per annum for a commercial registered address and corporate secretarial agent in Seoul or Busan
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 - USD 18,000 per annum for a full Korean K-IFRS statutory audit if the threshold is triggered; not applicable if the Yuhan Hoesa remains below the statutory audit threshold

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% national corporate income tax plus 10% local income tax surcharge, yielding an aggregate 27.5% headline rate for a resident Korean Yuhan Hoesa LLC.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Eligibility for R&D tax credits (up to 50% of qualifying software-development research expenses for SMEs under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act), Foreign Investment Promotion Act incentives (tariff exemptions and capital-good tax credits for foreign-invested high-tech enterprises), venture-enterprise tax reductions, and special temporary investment tax credits for strategic industries. Korea does not maintain a general patent box, but income from internally developed software IP may qualify for R&D credits and the special reserve for technology development.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Base and Tax Computation Return, with the Financial Accounts Schedule and Annex Schedule Set (NTS form package for corporate tax), filed electronically through the National Tax Service HomeTax portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: No later than 3 months after the fiscal year-end under Corporate Tax Act Article 60. For a December 31 fiscal year-end, the statutory deadline is March 31 of the following year; an automatic one-month extension is available where the return is prepared and signed by a certified tax accountant or CPA.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification and corporate status: business registration number, legal name, registered address, representative director, fiscal year, corporate classification (domestic vs foreign corporation), and tax office.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Korean Yuhan Hoesa owned by non-residents, disclose the full foreign-investment chain and ultimate shareholders. Non-resident directors must report their foreign tax identification numbers; the form must state whether the Korean entity has its place of effective management in Korea. A shell with no Korean management office creates immediate PE and substance red flags.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross business revenue: all sales from ISIC 6202 offshore software engineering, maintenance, consulting, and related digital-content services recognized under Korean GAAP on the accrual basis.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not net intercompany or offshore development center service fees. Revenue from foreign clients is Korean-source taxable business income where the active business or permanent establishment test is satisfied. If a portion of engineering is performed abroad, attach an allocation schedule with the OECD authorized OECD approach and support the profit split with headcount and payroll evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating expenses and cost of sales: employee salaries, social-insurance contributions, subcontractor engineering fees, cloud infrastructure, office rent, depreciation, and development tooling.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments to non-resident subcontractors, cloud providers, and related parties must be supported by contracts, invoices, and withholding records. Deductibility is denied for excessive remuneration to non-resident directors, undocumented entertainment expenses, and back-to-back service arrangements lacking business purpose. Transfer pricing documentation must substantiate each intercompany cost allocation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-operating income and expenses: interest income, dividends, foreign-exchange gains and losses, bad-debt recovery, and asset disposal gains.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Korea-sourced interest, royalties, dividends, and other gross income paid to non-residents must be separately scheduled with the 20% national withholding tax plus 10% local surtax (22% aggregate). Include the geographic-source allocation for non-resident payees and reconcile all foreign-exchange adjustments with bank records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income adjustments: add-backs and deductions reconciling pre-tax accounting profit to the corporate tax base, including transfer pricing adjustments, thin-capitalization interest disallowance, excessive debt, R&D supe-deductions, foreign tax credits, and carried-forward losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the Transfer Pricing Adjustment Statement for every cross-border related-party transaction. For a routine offshore development center functioning as a contract service provider, TNMM with a full-cost mark-up is the presumptive method; if CUP, resale price, cost-plus, or profit split is used, fully document the comparability analysis and arm's length range. Any non-arm's-length shifting will be adjusted with penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate tax computation: progressive national CIT rates, local income tax surcharge, foreign tax credits, minimum tax, prepayments, and final tax payable or refund.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders do not compute their tax in this box, but dividend declarations from retained earnings may trigger immediate withholding. If foreign taxes are claimed as credits, attach the Foreign Tax Credit Statement and proof of tax payment from each treaty jurisdiction. No credit is allowed for taxes paid by a disregarded branch or shell conduit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholding, reporting, and disclosure of payments to non-residents: dividends, interest, royalties, service fees, rents, and technical service charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: List every non-resident payee, jurisdiction of tax residence, Tax Residency Certificate details, beneficial-ownership certification, treaty article, reduced rate, and Korean tax withheld. The reduced treaty rate is available only if the payee is the beneficial owner and satisfies the limitation-on-benefits clause; otherwise backup withholding at 22% must be remitted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Related-party disclosure and economic-substance annex: Local File, Master File notification, Country-by-Country Report status, functional analysis, and Core Income-Generating Activities schedule.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For an offshore development center, attach the functional, asset, and risk analysis demonstrating Korean employees, premises, payroll, R&D decisions, and software IP development. If this annex states that the Korean entity has no office, no staff, and no active decision-making, the tax authorities will disregard the corporate form and recharacterize the Korean entity as a sham or dependent-agent permanent establishment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or non-filing triggers a 20% penalty on the unpaid corporate tax and a daily late-payment surcharge of approximately 0.022% (about 8.03% per annum), plus loss of certain deductions and carryforwards. Dishonest underreporting or fraudulent evasion triggers a 40% penalty on the understated tax. Criminal sanctions under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act include imprisonment of up to 3 years (up to 5 years when the evaded amount exceeds KRW 500 million) and fines of up to 3 times the evaded tax. Failure to prepare, maintain, or submit transfer pricing documentation or a Tax Residency Certificate can additionally trigger 30%-40% transaction penalties and denial of treaty benefits.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% national dividend withholding tax plus 2% local income tax surcharge, for a 22% aggregate statutory rate on non-resident shareholders. Qualifying dividends paid to resident corporate shareholders may be exempt under the corporate dividend exemption regime.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The Korean payer must obtain, before making the distribution, a Tax Residency Certificate issued by the tax authority of the non-resident's residence, a beneficial-ownership certificate, and a statement of entitlement to the bilateral treaty. The payer then submits the Application for Reduction or Exemption of Withholding Tax under Tax Treaties through HomeTax, attaching the dividend resolution, shareholding history, and TRC. If the reduced rate is not applied at source, the non-resident may file a refund claim with the District Tax Office within 3 years under the National Tax Basic Act, providing proof of Korean tax withheld, TRC, and beneficial-ownership evidence.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates on interest and royalties paid to non-residents are 20% plus 2% local surtax, totaling 22% absent treaty relief. Under typical OECD-based Korean DTAs, interest is reduced to 10%-15% and royalties to 10%-15%, with portfolio dividends at 15% and direct dividends at 5%-10% depending on shareholding thresholds and holding-period conditions.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Under the International Tax Adjustment Act, the Local File is mandatory where aggregate cross-border related-party transactions exceed KRW 10 billion in the taxable year; Master File preparation is required for Korean groups with annual consolidated revenue of KRW 100 billion or more, and Country-by-Country reporting applies where the multinational group's consolidated revenue reaches KRW 1 trillion. The NTS may still request contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation below those thresholds based on transaction risk and comparability indicators.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Korea does not operate a statutory offshore Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) code of the type seen in certain financial centers, but the substance-over-form and GAAR doctrines under the Corporate Tax Act and OECD BEPS Action 6 require an Offshore Development Center to maintain genuine presence in Korea: substantive employees, premises, payroll, board meetings, management, and Core Income-Generating Activities. The CIGA standard under applicable treaty Article 7 attributes profits to the Korean permanent establishment only where key entrepreneurial and R&D decisions are made in Korea. A shell with passive directors and no CIGA will be disregarded, treaty relief will be denied, and income will be reallocated to the ultimate shareholders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion, Shell Company Arrangement, and Revenue Understatement in Offshore Development Center
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting Korean-source engineering service revenue, billing the Korean ODC at below-cost through inflated offshore subcontractor invoices, keeping the entity as a paper shell with no physical office, employees, board meetings, or substantive operations, and moving profits to foreign shareholders through Wise, Payoneer, or wire without proper booking.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Corporate Tax Act assessment adding unreported income and disallowing sham deductions; 40% dishonest-unfiled penalty on the understated tax; 10% local income tax surcharge; International Tax Adjustment Act TP documentation penalties; criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act with imprisonment or fine up to 3 times the evaded tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Korea's corporate veil will be pierced where the LLC is a sham or alter ego of its shareholders. Directors face civil asset restitution, joint personal liability to the Korean tax authority under Commercial Act Article 401, travel blacklisting for unpaid taxes exceeding KRW 100 million, and criminal imprisonment up to 3 years, increased to up to 5 years when evaded tax exceeds KRW 500 million.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Abuse of Bilateral Double Tax Treaty Relief and False Beneficial Ownership
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing Korean dividends, royalties, or interest through an intermediary jurisdiction such as Singapore, Hong Kong, or the UAE without offices, personnel, or core income-generating activities, solely to claim a reduced DTA withholding rate unavailable to the ultimate shareholder, and submitting fabricated Tax Residency Certificates or beneficial-ownership declarations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of the DTA relief under the limitation-on-benefits and GAAR rules; recharacterization of the payments as made to the ultimate non-resident shareholder; imposition of the full 22% aggregate withholding tax plus 40% underreporting penalty, interest, and local surcharge; criminal tax-evasion fines of up to 3 times the tax at risk for false documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false beneficial-ownership or TRC certificates are personally liable for the under-withheld corporate taxes, subject to civil damages, asset freezes, and travel blacklisting; they face criminal imprisonment of 3 to 5 years for tax fraud, and officers of both the Korean payer and the foreign conduit may face cross-border mutual-assistance and extradition exposure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML and Foreign Exchange Evasion on Profit Repatriation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Remitting dividends, management fees, or engineering-service profits to foreign shareholders without a Foreign Exchange Transactions Act reporting or repatriation record, using Wise_B2B, Payoneer, or private wire accounts as concealed payment rails to bypass Korean bank foreign-exchange reporting, and failing to disclose foreign bank accounts or overseas equity interests.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Foreign Exchange Transactions Act: imprisonment of up to 5 years or fine up to KRW 200 million for unregistered international remittance. Financial Transactions Reports Act penalties apply for failure to file unusual-transaction or suspicious-transaction reports. The NTS may add 20%-40% of the undisclosed income as an unfounded penalty and impose daily surcharges on unpaid tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for restitution of the illegally remitted corporate profits; they face criminal fines, travel bans/passport revocation under tax arrears enforcement, and imprisonment of up to 5 years. Where the corporate form was used as a facade for personal profit shifting, civil veil-piercing makes directors jointly liable for all repatriated amounts and the associated tax penalties.
